statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases to 20% at the lower edge of the watch band as the index retraces, while Stress 54% stays elevated on multi-decade yield highs.
recommendation: The Nasdaq-100 has recovered roughly 207 points from its post-open low to trade near the top of its session range, while the 10-year and 30-year yields print at today's highs. Yields extending without the index confirming is a divergence rather than the aligned one-way path this contract measures, so Tail falls from 24% to 20%. The narrow published danger window covers the 17:00Z seven-year note auction and its first hour of digestion.
headline: Nasdaq-100 retraces to session highs while long-end yields extend, a divergence that eases Tail
body:
NDX cash trades near 30,411, about -0.19% on the day, inside a 30,204 to 30,449 session range roughly three hours into the US cash day. The index opened at 30,225, set its 30,204 low immediately after the open, and has since recovered to within 38 points of the session high. NQ December futures near 30,705 (-0.20%) sit 335 points above the 30,370 overnight low inside a 30,370-30,813 range. VIX near 16.17 is up about 6.5% but remains below its 16.57 session high, and the semiconductor proxy SMH at 596.99 (-0.74%) trades near the top of its own 588.92-598.77 range.

The rate and commodity backdrop has not improved. The 10-year yield at 5.17% and the 30-year at 5.46% both print at the top of today's 5.09-5.17 and 5.39-5.46 ranges, the highest levels since 2007 and 2004 respectively, while the 2-year at 4.908% is up only about 1.3 basis points, so the move remains a bear steepening rather than a front-end repricing. WTI crude near $94.59 is up about 2.63% with Brent near $105.76, after Houthi attacks on Saudi military sites, a Saudi interception of missiles aimed at Yanbu, and Iranian statements on restricting Strait of Hormuz navigation. Oil has nonetheless eased from the $95.89 area seen an hour earlier. Today's data ran strong across the board: initial jobless claims for the week ending September 19 printed 197,000 against a 201,000 consensus, August new home sales came in at a 684,000 annual rate against 620,000 expected, and the Kansas Fed composite index reached 14 against a consensus of 5. New York Fed President Williams called a further increase by year end reasonable and Philadelphia's Paulson said some modest further tightening may be warranted. Treasury Secretary Bessent announced a two-month extension of the US-China trade truce to January 10. Shared Finviz context collected at 12:21Z is more than four hours old and therefore stale under the provider contract, and its futures and calendar sections were unavailable, so it is used here only for headline discovery and latest-session breadth tone, not as current evidence.

The question this contract asks is whether the price path is denying retracement, and today it plainly is not. The session low was set within minutes of the open and has been recovered rather than extended, which is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that defines Tail. Yields and oil sit near session extremes while the index sits near the top of its range, a divergence rather than the aligned amplifier stack that would justify the block band. Tail therefore eases from 24% to 20%, remaining in the watch band because the long end is still making new highs and the 17:00Z seven-year auction is an unresolved checkpoint into a 22-year yield peak. Stress eases only modestly to 54%, reflecting an environment that is genuinely difficult but is still mean-reverting.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours held a yellow plateau near 20-24% Tail through Wednesday's US afternoon and evening, eased to three green hours between 01:00Z and 03:00Z as Asian trade stayed orderly, and rebuilt from the European open. Risk peaked at 25% Tail and 58% Stress at 09:00Z as the 30-year yield pushed to a post-2004 high, then oscillated in a 21-24% band through the US pre-market and opening hours without ever establishing persistent one-way structure. Stress ranged between 49% and 58% throughout, the signature of a difficult but still mean-reverting environment.
outlookSummary: Tail is published in the watch band through the remainder of the US session, stepping to 24% for the single 17:00Z hour covering the seven-year note auction, which is the narrow published danger window. It eases through auction digestion, the power hour and the cash close, then falls into the 16-19% green band overnight once the scheduled calendar is exhausted. Risk rebuilds gradually from the European pre-market on Friday toward 23% around the 12:30Z durable goods release, the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z final Michigan sentiment reading. Confidence decays from 87% to 78% with distance from the assessment time. Every forecast hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not an assertion that future price structure has been observed.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NDX 30,411 has retraced to within 38 points of its 30,449 session high after opening near the 30,204 low, while the 10y at 5.17% and 30y at 5.46% both print at today's highs. Yields extend, equities do not confirm, and that non-confirmation is why Tail eases from 24 to 20.

forecast.analysis: The 17:00Z seven-year note auction is the hour's scheduled checkpoint and the published danger window, with the 30y at a 22-year high into it. Tail is lifted to the top of the watch band for the unresolved auction only; a weak result would be the credible route to a delayed long-end second leg, and an orderly one would not.
drivers: 7-Year Note Auction at 17:00Z lands with 30y yield at a 2004 high
Auction tail or weak indirect bid is the conditional long-end trigger
Pre-event alignment is not counted as observed price-path evidence
Published danger window covers 17:00Z to 18:00Z

forecast.analysis: Auction digestion hour. If the seven-year result clears without a material tail, the conditional path is long-end stabilisation and continued index retracement; if the long end extends instead, repeated failure of pullbacks would be the structure to watch. Neither outcome is observed at this assessment time.
drivers: Conditional: orderly auction digestion allows Stress to begin decaying
Conditional: a further long-end leg would be the Tail amplifier
Semis proxy SMH -0.74% sits near the top of its session range
Bear-steepening so far, with 2y only +1.3bp at 4.908%

forecast.analysis: US power hour into 20:00Z. Late-session continuation or reversal is the conditional risk, with month-end and quarter-end rebalancing flows approaching. Tail eases as the auction checkpoint passes, assuming no fresh long-end extension emerges during the hour.
drivers: Power hour 19:00Z-20:00Z carries late-session continuation risk
Conditional: close near session highs would confirm retracement worked
Quarter-end rebalancing approaches into next week

forecast.analysis: US cash close at 20:00Z. Settlement and the transition to the futures-only session typically reduce directional efficiency. The published scores assume the session resolves without a new one-way leg; an unusually weak close would be the invalidation of that assumption.
drivers: US cash close 20:00Z, settlement and index rebalancing prints
Conditional: a close in the upper half of the range caps Tail
Liquidity thins as cash equity participation ends

forecast.analysis: First post-close futures hour. With the scheduled US calendar exhausted for the day, conditional risk falls into the green band: overnight NQ trade is normally range-bound absent a fresh geopolitical headline, and Middle East developments remain the main unscheduled route to a gap.
drivers: Scheduled US calendar exhausted after the cash close
Unscheduled Middle East headline risk remains the overnight route to a gap
Thin post-close liquidity generally favours range behaviour

forecast.analysis: Late US evening futures trade before Asia. Conditional risk stays in the green band as volatility typically decays into the handover. Oil remains the cross-asset to watch given Strait of Hormuz navigation rhetoric, though nothing further has been reported at this assessment time.
drivers: Volatility normally decays into the Asia handover
Oil the key overnight cross-asset after the +2.63% WTI session
No scheduled US release during this hour

forecast.analysis: Asian session opening hour. Conditional path is orderly two-way trade; regional equity reaction to the US long-end move is the checkpoint. A sustained bid for duration in Asia would relieve the amplifier stack, while a further yield extension would rebuild it.
drivers: Asia opens and reacts to the US long-end repricing
Checkpoint: Asian demand for duration relieves or extends the yield move
JGB long end is the usual overnight transmission channel

forecast.analysis: Asian mid-session. Absent a new catalyst the conditional expectation is continued range behaviour with normal retracement, which is the environment this contract treats as benign. Published scores would be invalidated by a one-way Asian leg carrying into the European handover.
drivers: No scheduled US macro release during Asian mid-session
Invalidation: a one-way Asian leg persisting into Europe
Range behaviour with normal retracement is the base case

forecast.analysis: Quietest part of the 24-hour cycle. Conditional risk is published at its lowest for the horizon because scheduled catalysts are absent and Asian liquidity is past its opening burst. This is a projection of conditional risk, not an observation of overnight structure.
drivers: Lowest scheduled-catalyst density of the forecast horizon
Asian opening liquidity burst has passed
Conditional projection only; no overnight structure observed yet

forecast.analysis: Asian close approaching. Conditional risk remains in the green band. The handover into European pre-market is the next structural checkpoint, where the overnight yield path and any Middle East headlines would first be repriced into NQ.
drivers: Asian close and European pre-market handover approaching
Checkpoint: overnight yield path repriced at the European handover
Green-band conditional risk with catalysts absent

forecast.analysis: European pre-market hours. Conditional risk begins a gradual rebuild as European rates desks engage with the US long-end move. Bund and gilt opening levels are the checkpoint, given that yesterday's and today's selloff has been a global rather than purely US phenomenon.
drivers: European rates desks engage with the US long-end move
Checkpoint: Bund and gilt opening levels set the global tone
Conditional rebuild from the overnight low in risk

forecast.analysis: Continued European pre-market. The conditional path assumes an orderly European rates open. Sterling's recent weakness and the global scope of the bond move mean a disorderly European long-end session is the identified route to a higher Tail reading than published here.
drivers: Conditional: orderly European rates open assumed in the published score
Global bond move means European long end can re-transmit to NQ
Route to a higher reading is a disorderly European session

forecast.analysis: European cash equity open approaches. Conditional risk continues rebuilding toward the watch band. The checkpoint is whether European equities follow the index recovery seen in the US afternoon or instead re-price the higher global yield structure downward.
drivers: European cash equity open approaches
Checkpoint: European equities follow the US recovery or fade it
Conditional rebuild toward the watch band

forecast.analysis: European open hour. Conditional risk sits at the top of the green band. This is the first session of the forecast horizon where genuine directional structure could form, though none is observed at this assessment time and the published score is conditional only.
drivers: European cash open is the first real directional checkpoint of the horizon
No structure observed yet; the published score is conditional
Top of the green band ahead of the watch-band rebuild

forecast.analysis: European morning. Conditional risk crosses into the watch band as two-way flow builds. The assumed path is mixed, with equity and rates signals capable of diverging as they have today; an aligned European selloff would be the condition for a higher reading.
drivers: Two-way European flow builds through the morning
Assumed mixed regime, equities and rates capable of diverging
Condition for a higher reading: an aligned European selloff

forecast.analysis: European mid-morning. Conditional risk continues its gradual rebuild toward the Friday US session. The Friday calendar carries durable goods at 12:30Z and the final Michigan sentiment reading at 14:00Z, both of which feed the same growth-and-inflation repricing driving this week's yields.
drivers: Friday durable goods at 12:30Z is the next scheduled US checkpoint
Michigan final sentiment at 14:00Z follows in the US morning
Gradual conditional rebuild toward the US session

forecast.analysis: European late morning. Conditional risk holds in the lower watch band. Positioning ahead of the Friday US data pair typically reduces directional conviction rather than creating one-way structure, which is why the score is held rather than raised further.
drivers: Positioning ahead of the Friday US data pair
Pre-data positioning normally reduces conviction, not raises Tail
Lower watch band held rather than raised

forecast.analysis: European midday. Conditional risk is unchanged from the previous hour. The overlap window before the US pre-market is generally the quietest part of the European session, and no scheduled US release falls in this hour.
drivers: Quietest part of the European session before US pre-market
No scheduled US release in this hour
Conditional score unchanged from the prior hour

forecast.analysis: US pre-market opens. Conditional risk holds in the watch band with the 12:30Z durable goods release in the next hour. Stress edges higher to reflect the approaching data rather than any observed change in price-path structure.
drivers: US pre-market begins ahead of the 12:30Z durable goods release
Stress edges up on approaching data, not on observed structure
Watch-band conditional risk maintained

forecast.analysis: Durable goods orders for August print at 12:30Z within this hour. Under the private-calibration principle applied here, a surprise in either direction primarily raises Stress and informs Confidence; Tail would only follow if the subsequent price path denied retracement, which cannot be known now.
drivers: Durable Goods Orders (AUG) released at 12:30Z in this hour
A data surprise primarily raises Stress, not Tail, before the path is seen
Tail would follow only on an observed no-retracement path

forecast.analysis: Friday US cash open at 13:30Z falls in this hour. The opening auction and its immediate continuation are the highest-value Tail evidence of the horizon, as today's own session demonstrated when the post-open low was recovered rather than extended.
drivers: US cash open 13:30Z; opening auction is the key Tail evidence
Today's post-open low was recovered, not extended
Conditional: shallow pullbacks after the open would raise Tail
